Key Takeaways

  • Property has two numbers that matter: the market value and the government guidance (registration) value.
  • A documented valuation supports loan applications, fair pricing, dispute settlements and NRI decisions.
  • We assess location, extent, comparable transactions and guidance value to arrive at a defensible figure.
  • Useful before buying, selling, mortgaging, or dividing property among heirs.
  • Delivered as a written valuation report.

Whether you're buying, selling, taking a loan or settling property among family, you need to know what it's actually worth — not just what the other side claims.

JaaGa provides a professional valuation that considers location, extent, condition, comparable sales and the government guidance value, delivered as a clear written report.

When You Need a Valuation

Before buying or selling, to price fairly and avoid over- or under-paying.

For a loan or loan-against-property file, and for inheritance, partition or dispute settlements where a defensible value is needed.

How We Value the Property

  1. 1

    Property Details

    We collect the location, extent, type, age and condition of the property.

  2. 2

    Market & Guidance Study

    We study comparable transactions and the applicable government guidance value.

  3. 3

    Assessment

    We arrive at market and guidance-value figures with the reasoning behind them.

  4. 4

    Valuation Report

    You receive a documented valuation report suitable for your purpose.

Documents Required

  • Property location and survey/plot number
  • Extent and built-up area
  • Property type and age/condition
  • Existing deed (if available)
  • Purpose of valuation

Common Problems We Solve

Guidance vs market gap

The registration value often differs sharply from the market. We report both and explain the gap.

Thin comparables

Some micro-markets have few recent sales. We widen the comparison sensibly.

Dispute-grade defensibility

For settlements and courts, the figure must be reasoned. We document the basis.

Why Property Valuation Matters

Pricing a property on rumour or a broker's number is how people over-pay when buying and under-sell when selling. A reasoned valuation gives you a defensible figure to negotiate, borrow, settle or decide against.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the difference between market value and guidance value?

Market value is what the property realistically sells for; guidance (registration) value is the government's minimum value for stamp duty. They often differ, and both matter.

Can I use the report for a bank loan?

The report supports loan discussions; banks may also require their own empanelled valuer, and we advise on this.

Do you value both land and flats?

Yes — open plots, agricultural land, houses and apartments.

Is this useful for family settlements?

Very. A documented, reasoned value helps divide property fairly and reduces disputes.

Can NRIs get this remotely?

Yes. Share the property details and purpose and we deliver the report digitally.
